problems.question: What is the value of \[ \begin{aligned} &1{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000 \\ &\quad {}- 777{,}777{,}777{,}777? \end{aligned} \]
hints: Work from the right: the units digits must add to \(10\) with a carry, and every other column then adds to \(10\) with that carry
problems.solution: Lining up the subtraction gives \[ \begin{aligned} &1{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000 \\ &\quad {}- 777{,}777{,}777{,}777 \\ &= 222{,}222{,}222{,}223. \end{aligned} \] Equivalently, to climb from \(777{,}777{,}777{,}777\) up to \(1{,}000{,}000{,}000{,}000\) you add \(3\) in the units place and \(2\) in each of the other eleven places. Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question: What is the value of \[\frac{16+8}{4-2}?\]
hints: The fraction bar groups the whole numerator over the whole denominator
Simplify \(16+8\) and \(4-2\) separately before dividing
problems.solution: \[\frac{16+8}{4-2} = \frac{24}{2} = 12.\] Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question: Two hundred thousand times two hundred thousand equals
hints: Write two hundred thousand as \(200{,}000\)
Multiply the leading digits, then count the zeros: each factor has five zeros
problems.solution: \(200{,}000 \times 200{,}000\) \(= 4 \times 10^{10}\) \(= 40{,}000{,}000{,}000,\) which is forty billion. Thus, the correct answer is E .

problems.question: If \(991 + 993 + 995\) \(+ 997 + 999\) \(= 5000 - N,\) then \(N = \)
hints: Each of the five numbers is just a little less than \(1000\)
Write each as \(1000 - k;\) the sum becomes \(5000 - (9+7+5+3+1)\)

problems.question: A “domino” is made up of two small squares: . Which of the “checkerboards” illustrated below CANNOT be covered exactly and completely by a whole number of non-overlapping dominoes?
hints: Each domino covers exactly two small squares, so focus on how many small squares each board has.
A board can be fully covered only if its total number of squares is even; find the number of squares in each board by multiplying its two dimensions.
problems.solution: Every domino covers exactly \(2\) squares, so any board that is completely covered by non-overlapping dominoes must contain an even number of small squares. Counting squares: \(3 \times 4 = 12,\) \(3 \times 5 = 15,\) \(4 \times 4 = 16,\) \(4 \times 5 = 20,\) and \(6 \times 3 = 18.\) Only \(3 \times 5 = 15\) is odd, so that board cannot be covered. (Each of the even boards has a side of even length and is easily tiled with dominoes.) Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question:
Which number in the array below is both the largest in its column and the smallest in its row? (Columns go up and down, rows go right and left.)

\[\begin{array}{ccccc} 10 & 6 & 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 11 & 7 & 14 & 10 & 8 \\ 8 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 9 \\ 13 & 4 & 15 & 12 & 1 \\ 8 & 2 & 5 & 9 & 3 \end{array}\]
hints: First find the largest number in each of the five columns
Then check which of those column-maxima is also the smallest number in its own row
problems.solution: The largest entry in each column is \(13\) (column \(1\)), \(7\) (column \(2\)), \(15\) (column \(3\)), \(12\) (column \(4\)), and \(9\) (column \(5\)). Of these, only \(7\) is the smallest number in its own row (row \(2\) is \(11,\) \(7,\) \(14,\) \(10,\) \(8\)). Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question: The value of \[\tiny\frac{(487{,}000)(12{,}027{,}300) + (9{,}621{,}001)(487{,}000)}{(19{,}367)(0.05)}\] is closest to
hints: The numerator shares a common factor of \(487{,}000\)
Round each number to a single leading digit before dividing, for example \(487{,}000 \approx 500{,}000\) and \((19{,}367)(0.05) \approx 1000\)
problems.solution: Factor the numerator: \(487{,}000\) \(\cdot\, (12{,}027{,}300 + 9{,}621{,}001).\) Rounding to leading digits, this is about \(500{,}000\) \(\times (10{,}000{,}000 + 10{,}000{,}000)\) \(= 500{,}000 \times 2\) \(\times 10^{7}.\) The denominator is about \(20{,}000 \times 0.05 = 1000.\) So the value is roughly \(\dfrac{500{,}000 \times 2 \times 10^{7}}{1000}\) \(= 10^{10}\) \(= 10{,}000{,}000{,}000.\) Thus, the correct answer is D .

problems.question: What is the largest quotient that can be formed using two numbers chosen from the set \(\{-24, -3, -2, 1, 2, 8\}?\)
hints: A quotient is largest when it is positive and large in size
A negative divided by a negative is positive; try the largest-magnitude negative over the smallest-magnitude negative
problems.solution: For a large quotient it should be positive, so use two positive numbers or two negative numbers. Best positive pair: \(\dfrac{8}{1} = 8.\) Best negative pair: \(\dfrac{-24}{-2} = 12.\) The larger is \(12.\) Thus, the correct answer is D .

problems.question: How many whole numbers from \(1\) through \(46\) are divisible by either \(3\) or \(5\) or both?
hints: Count the multiples of \(3\) and the multiples of \(5\) separately
Numbers divisible by both \(3\) and \(5\) are multiples of \(15\) and get counted twice, so subtract them once
problems.solution: There are \(15\) multiples of \(3\) and \(9\) multiples of \(5\) up to \(46.\) The \(3\) multiples of \(15\) (namely \(15,\) \(30,\) \(45\)) were counted twice. By inclusion-exclusion, the count is \(15 + 9 - 3 = 21.\) Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question: The area in square units of the region enclosed by parallelogram \(ABCD\) is
hints: Take \(\overline{BC}\) as the base; it is horizontal from \(B(0,2)\) to \(C(4,2)\)
The area is base times height, where the height is the vertical distance between the two horizontal sides
problems.solution: Side \(BC\) runs from \((0,2)\) to \((4,2),\) so the base is \(4.\) The opposite side \(AD\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so the height is \(2.\) The area is \(4 \times 2 = 8.\) Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question: There are several sets of three different numbers whose sum is \(15\) which can be chosen from \(\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}.\) How many of these sets contain a \(5?\)
hints: If \(5\) is one of the three numbers, the other two must add to \(10\)
List the pairs of different numbers from \(\{1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9\}\) that sum to \(10\)
problems.solution: With \(5\) chosen, the other two different numbers must sum to \(10.\) The pairs are \(1+9,\) \(2+8,\) \(3+7,\) \(4+6,\) giving \(4\) sets. Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question: If \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{2+3+4}{3} \\ &= \frac{1990+1991+1992}{N}, \end{aligned} \] then \(N = \)
hints: Simplify the left side first
The sum of three consecutive integers divided by the middle one equals \(3\)
problems.solution: The left side is \(\dfrac{9}{3} = 3.\) The right side is \(\dfrac{5973}{N},\) and setting it equal to \(3\) gives \(N = 1991.\) Equivalently, \((k-1) + k + (k+1) = 3k,\) so dividing by \(3\) leaves the middle term. Here the middle term is \(1991.\) Thus, the correct answer is D .

problems.question: How many zeros are at the end of the product \[ \begin{aligned} &25 \times 25 \times 25 \times 25 \\ &\quad {}\times 25 \times 25 \times 25 \\ &\quad {}\times 8 \times 8 \times 8? \end{aligned} \]
hints: A trailing zero comes from a factor of \(10 = 2 \times 5\)
Count the total factors of \(2\) and of \(5;\) the number of trailing zeros is the smaller count
problems.solution: Since \(25 = 5^2,\) the seven \(25\)’s give \(5^{14}.\) Since \(8 = 2^3,\) the three \(8\)’s give \(2^9.\) The number of trailing zeros is \(\min(14, 9) = 9.\) Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question: Several students are competing in a series of three races. A student earns \(5\) points for winning a race, \(3\) points for finishing second, and \(1\) point for finishing third. There are no ties. What is the smallest number of points that a student must earn in the three races to be guaranteed of earning more points than any other student?
hints: To be guaranteed the lead, plan for the worst case where another student does as well as possible
Check the attainable three-race totals in increasing order; for each one, see whether the remaining places allow a rival to tie or exceed it
problems.solution: A total of \(11\) (for example \(5+5+1\)) does not guarantee first place, since another student could also reach \(11.\) But if one student scores \(5+5+3 = 13,\) the remaining places give every other student at most \(3+3+5 = 11.\) So \(13\) points guarantees the lead. Thus, the correct answer is D .

problems.question: All six sides of a rectangular solid were rectangles. A one-foot cube was cut out of the rectangular solid as shown. The total number of square feet in the surface of the new solid is how many more or less than that of the original solid?
hints: Cutting the cube removes some faces that were on the surface but uncovers new ones; compare the two amounts
The cube’s top, front, and back faces were on the surface (\(3\) square feet removed); the notch’s floor and its two side walls become new surface (\(3\) square feet added)
problems.solution: The removed cube had three faces on the surface of the solid (top, front, and back), so \(3\) square feet of surface are removed. Cutting it out exposes three new faces (the floor of the notch and its two side walls), adding \(3\) square feet. The surface area is unchanged. Thus, the correct answer is C .

hints: After each fold, track which squares end up on the bottom (or top) of the stack
Folds \(1\) and \(2\) leave the middle rows; folds \(3\) and \(4\) leave the middle columns, and the final left-over-right fold flips square \(9\) to the top
problems.solution: Fold \(1\) (top over bottom) leaves squares \(9\text{–}16\) on the bottom. Fold \(2\) (bottom over top) leaves \(9\text{–}12\) on the bottom. Fold \(3\) (right over left) leaves \(9\) and \(10\) on the bottom. Fold \(4\) (left over right) puts \(10\) on the bottom and brings \(9\) to the top. Thus, the correct answer is B .

problems.question: An auditorium with \(20\) rows of seats has \(10\) seats in the first row. Each successive row has one more seat than the previous row. If students taking an exam are permitted to sit in any row, but not next to another student in that row, then the maximum number of students that can be seated for an exam is
hints: In a row of \(n\) seats, the most students with no two adjacent is \(\left\lceil \frac{n}{2} \right\rceil\)
Row \(k\) has \(9+k\) seats; add \(\left\lceil \frac{9+k}{2} \right\rceil\) over the \(20\) rows
problems.solution: Row \(k\) has \(9+k\) seats, so it holds \(\left\lceil \frac{9+k}{2} \right\rceil\) students. For rows \(1\) through \(20\) (seats \(10\) through \(29\)) the maxima are \(5,\) \(6,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) \(8,\) \(\ldots,\) \(14,\) \(14,\) \(15.\) These sum to \(200.\) Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question: The vertical axis indicates the number of employees, but the scale was accidentally omitted from this graph. What percent of the employees at the Gauss Company have worked there for \(5\) years or more?
hints: Since the vertical scale is unknown, work with the number of X’s rather than any value
Divide the X’s over years \(5\) through \(10\) by the total number of X’s
problems.solution: No matter the missing scale, each X represents the same number of employees. There are \(9\) X’s over years \(5\) through \(10,\) and \(30\) X’s in all. So the fraction is \(\dfrac{9}{30} = 30\%.\) Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question: The average (arithmetic mean) of \(10\) different positive whole numbers is \(10.\) The largest possible value of any of these numbers is
hints: The ten numbers must sum to \(10 \times 10 = 100\)
To make one number as large as possible, make the other nine as small as possible: \(1, 2, \ldots, 9\)
problems.solution: The ten numbers sum to \(100.\) To maximize one of them, the other nine (all different positive whole numbers) should be as small as possible: \(1 + 2 + \cdots + 9 = 45.\) The largest number is then \(100 - 45 = 55.\) Thus, the correct answer is C .

problems.question:
In the addition problem shown, each digit has been replaced by a letter. If different letters represent different digits, then \(C = \)

\[\begin{array}{cccc} & A & B & C \\ & & A & B \\ + & & & A \\ \hline & 3 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\]
hints: Write the sum in terms of \(A, B, C\)
problems.solution: The three numbers add to \(111A + 11B + C = 300.\) Since \(A = 1\) is too small and \(A \ge 3\) is too large, \(A = 2.\) Then \(11B + C = 78,\) which forces \(B = 7\) and \(C = 1.\) So \(C = 1.\) Thus, the correct answer is A .

problems.question: For every \(3^\circ\) rise in temperature, the volume of a certain gas expands by \(4\) cubic centimeters. If the volume of the gas is \(24\) cubic centimeters when the temperature is \(32^\circ,\) what was the volume of the gas in cubic centimeters when the temperature was \(20^\circ?\)
hints: The temperature dropped from \(32^\circ\) to \(20^\circ,\) a change of \(12^\circ\)
Each \(3^\circ\) drop shrinks the volume by \(4\) cubic centimeters
problems.solution: From \(32^\circ\) to \(20^\circ\) is a \(12^\circ\) decrease, which is \(4\) steps of \(3^\circ.\) The volume decreases by \(4 \times 4 = 16\) cubic centimeters, from \(24\) down to \(24 - 16 = 8.\) Thus, the correct answer is A .

problems.question: Each spinner is divided into \(3\) equal parts. The results obtained from spinning the two spinners are multiplied. What is the probability that this product is an even number?
hints: A product is even unless both spun numbers are odd
Find the probability of an odd product (odd times odd), then subtract from \(1\)
problems.solution: The product is odd only when both numbers are odd. The first spinner is odd (\(1\) or \(3\)) with probability \(\dfrac23,\) and the second is odd (\(5\)) with probability \(\dfrac13.\) So the product is odd with probability \(\dfrac23 \times \dfrac13 = \dfrac29,\) and even with probability \(1 - \dfrac29 = \dfrac79.\) Thus, the correct answer is D .

problems.question: The Pythagoras High School band has \(100\) female and \(80\) male members. The Pythagoras High School orchestra has \(80\) female and \(100\) male members. There are \(60\) females who are members in both band and orchestra. Altogether, there are \(230\) students who are in either band or orchestra or both. The number of males in the band who are NOT in the orchestra is
hints: First find how many females are in at least one group, using \(100 + 80 - 60\)
Subtract the females from the \(230\) total to get the males in at least one group, then use inclusion–exclusion to find how many males are in both groups
problems.solution: Females in band or orchestra: \(100 + 80 - 60 = 120.\) So males in at least one group: \(230 - 120 = 110.\) With \(80\) males in band and \(100\) in orchestra, the males in both are \(80 + 100 - 110 = 70.\) Hence males in band but not orchestra: \(80 - 70 = 10.\) Thus, the correct answer is A .

problems.question: A cube of edge \(3\) cm is cut into \(N\) smaller cubes, not all the same size. If the edge of each of the smaller cubes is a whole number of centimeters, then \(N = \)
hints: The smaller cubes must have whole-number edges, so each is edge \(1\) or edge \(2\)
Only one edge-\(2\) cube fits; the rest are unit cubes filling the remaining volume \(27 - 8\)
problems.solution: The \(3 \times 3 \times 3\) cube has volume \(27.\) Since the cubes are smaller and have whole-number edge lengths, their edges are \(1\) or \(2\). Two edge-\(2\) cubes cannot be disjoint inside the original cube: separating them would require a total span of at least \(4\) in some direction. Thus at most one edge-\(2\) cube fits. The remaining \(27 - 8 = 19\) of volume is filled by \(19\) unit cubes. That is \(1 + 19 = 20\) cubes. Thus, the correct answer is E .

problems.question: An equilateral triangle is originally painted black. Each time the triangle is changed, the middle fourth of each black triangle turns white. After five changes, what fractional part of the original area of the black triangle remains black?
hints: After one change the middle fourth turns white, so \(\dfrac34\) of the black area remains
Each change multiplies the black area by \(\dfrac34,\) so after five changes multiply by \(\left(\dfrac34\right)^5\)
problems.solution: Each change leaves \(\dfrac34\) of the current black area black. After five changes the black fraction is \[\left(\dfrac34\right)^5 = \dfrac{243}{1024}.\] Thus, the correct answer is C .
